excerpt_i18n.en: Based on the current trend of accelerating across all sectors, the integration of AI into the health domain for ordinary people will proceed faster than anticipated, according to AI researcher Li Min. Recently, Wu Jingyi, a post-00s village doctor from Tushan Village in Jiujiang, Jiangxi, unexpectedly gained popularity online. Beyond being moved by her story of taking over her grandfather’s role as a village doctor and staying in the countryside, people were also pleasantly surprised by her innovative approach of using a mobile AI app to establish health records for over 200 elderly villagers, analyzing their blood pressure and pulse. Behind the viral spread of this small story is the fact that young people are beginning to use new technologies to improve the lives of the elderly. It suddenly became apparent that the application of AI in the health sector has already reached the most grassroots levels of rural areas. The mobile app used by Wu Jingyi is called "Ant Ah Fu," an AI health management application developed by Ant Group. Launched six months ago, it has surpassed 15 million monthly active users and answers over 5 million health-related questions from users daily. The development of the AI health track goes even further. In mid-2023, Shanghai’s top-tier Ruijin Hospital, a medical hub, suddenly announced a collaboration with Huawei to open-source a large pathology model. 01. Tech Giants Rush In, Giving Rise to an "AI Ah Fu" in the Health Track. The "first half" of AI development was dominated by the intelligence limits of general large models, while entering the "second half," the deep cultivation of vertical tracks such as law, finance, and healthcare, along with practical application effectiveness, is becoming the true deciding factor. According to Leifeng.com, since the beginning of this year, companies including overseas giants like OpenAI and Google, as well as domestic players such as Ant Group, Huawei, and Baichuan, have been rushing into the field.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según la tendencia actual de aceleración en todos los sectores, la integración de la IA en el ámbito de la salud de las personas comunes será más rápida de lo previsto, afirmó la investigadora de IA Li Min. Recientemente, Wu Jingyi, una médica rural nacida después del año 2000 de la aldea Tushan en Jiujiang, Jiangxi, se volvió inesperadamente popular en internet. Además de conmoverse por su historia de heredar el legado de su abuelo como médico rural y quedarse en el campo, la gente se sorprendió por su innovador método de usar la IA en su teléfono móvil para crear archivos de salud para más de 200 ancianos de la aldea, analizando su presión arterial y pulso. Detrás de este pequeño incidente que se hizo viral, está el hecho de que los jóvenes están comenzando a utilizar nuevas tecnologías para mejorar la vida de los ancianos.
